intended_object: A primitive ray class character: a character χ of the ray class group Cl_𝔪 of a number field (with 𝔪 a modulus that has a finite and an infinite part) is primitive if it does not factor through Cl_𝔫 → Cl_𝔪 for any proper divisor 𝔫 of 𝔪. Equivalently, its conductor equals 𝔪 (Neukirch VI §1). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
`RayClassCharacter 𝔪` is the type of homomorphisms `RayClassGroup 𝔪 →* ℂˣ`. For `𝔫 ∣ 𝔪`, the map `induced h` pulls a character back along the surjective transition map `classMap : Cl_𝔪 → Cl_𝔫`. A `Modulus` has two parts: a nonzero integral ideal (the finite part) and a finset of real places (the infinite part). Divisibility of moduli means the finite parts divide and the infinite parts are contained, which is the standard notion. Equality of moduli is componentwise (`Modulus.ext`).

So `IsPrimitive χ` says: whenever χ is pulled back from some ψ on a divisor 𝔫 of 𝔪, then 𝔫 = 𝔪. In other words, χ is not induced from any strictly smaller modulus, which is the textbook definition of primitivity (conductor = modulus).

Degenerate cases also behave correctly:
- Every character of the trivial modulus is primitive.
- The trivial character is primitive exactly when 𝔪 = 1.
- Real places are included in the condition, so a character that is trivial on the sign classes at a real place in 𝔪 counts as imprimitive, as the standard theory requires.

The setting (ray class groups of a number field) is the natural one for this notion. Mathlib has no ray class groups or ray class characters. Its `DirichletCharacter.IsPrimitive` is only the special case K = ℚ, phrased through ℤ/n, so it is not a more general counterpart.
